speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this cough and breathlessness, and does the shortness of breath occur with exertion or at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough has been going on for about six weeks, and the breathlessness definitely gets worse when I try to walk or do any exertion. speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the hospital policy, so we will rely on a detailed physical exam. Is your cough productive, and if so, what color is the sputum? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or chest pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, my cough is productive, and the sputum is white. I haven't noticed any swelling in my legs or any chest pain. I want to emphasize that, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That white sputum and lack of leg swelling make heart failure less likely. Have you noticed any fever, night sweats, or unintended weight loss over the past month? Also, do you have a known history of smoking or recent exposure to tuberculosis contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any fever, night sweats, or lost any weight recently. I do have a history of smoking; I quit about five years ago after thirty pack-years, but I don't know anyone with tuberculosis.
